HAND-SIZE ILLUSION

GOAL
Make one hand feel mentally larger without moving it.

ONE RULE
Keep the real hand visible and still.

PLAY
Look at one relaxed hand. For three seconds imagine its felt outline extending slightly beyond the real edges, then compare imagined and visible boundaries.

TWIST
Use only a small change; stop if it feels unsettling.

WIN
The body-image boundary and the visible hand can be noticed as separate representations.
rituals.fullRitual:
GAME
HAND-SIZE ILLUSION

GOAL
Make one hand feel mentally larger without moving it.

ONE RULE
Keep the real hand visible and still.

PLAY
Look at one relaxed hand. For three seconds imagine its felt outline extending slightly beyond the real edges, then compare imagined and visible boundaries.

TWIST
Use only a small change; stop if it feels unsettling.

WIN
The body-image boundary and the visible hand can be noticed as separate representations.

MIND BEND
An imagined hand can briefly feel visually larger while the real hand remains unchanged. Body-size representation is editable rather than a perfect copy of physical reality.

SAFETY
Keep this to a comfortable, harmless visual-body illusion. If concerning physical symptoms arise, abandon the exercise and seek appropriate medical assessment rather than using the illusion or attention shift as reassurance.

rituals.name: RETURN COST
rituals.unique_game_move: attend to one location, move away, then test the ease of returning attention to the previously visited location versus a fresh location
rituals.recognition_cue: Attention • Mental quiet. ROUTER TAGS: focus distracted attention grounding present restless mental quiet anchor focus distracted attention grounding present restless mental quiet anchor focus distracted attention grounding present restless mental quiet anchor
rituals.immediate_need: steady attention and return to the present
rituals.match_reason: Attention • Mental quiet; ATTENTION; ROUTER TAGS: focus distracted attention grounding present restless mental quiet anchor focus distracted attention grounding present restless mental quiet anchor focus distracted attention grounding present restless mental quiet anchor
rituals.goal: See whether attention treats a recently visited place differently.
rituals.mission: See whether attention treats a recently visited place differently.
rituals.rule: The eyes can stay still; only covert attention moves.
rituals.one_rule: The eyes can stay still; only covert attention moves.
rituals.play: Choose three visible points: LEFT, CENTRE, RIGHT. Attend LEFT for one beat, move to CENTRE for two beats, then compare how it feels to send attention back to LEFT versus onward to RIGHT.
rituals.twist: Do not stare harder at either side; compare only the attentional move.
rituals.win: Returning to a recently attended location feels measurably different from moving to a fresh one.
rituals.mindBend: Revisiting a location that attention touched moments ago can differ from shifting toward an untouched location. The deeper point is a residual cost or facilitation created by attentional history.
rituals.mind_bend: Revisiting a location that attention touched moments ago can differ from shifting toward an untouched location. The deeper point is a residual cost or facilitation created by attentional history.
rituals.safety: For one pass, use brief relaxed focus. If eye strain or headache appears, finish there and let your eyes focus normally.
